# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–13 (Complete – Updated 109)

## Setting and Time
- **Current Period**: Spring of fourth year in Mirecombe hill farms (Seena with aching back; Ellan Lindner humming childhood tune while scrubbing step; Maric counting coins twice, coming up penny short; son Isnar Brackwood born to Wevie Lindner and Madan Brackwood). Earlier: Winter of third year with frost on hedges. Even earlier: Evening at Brighton following Dobbin's arrival; fine brilliant moonlight night of May, warm and balmy. Army ordered to Belgium before week's end; mobilization imminent from Chatham. Embarkation completed: transports left Chatham two days after Mrs. O'Dowd's party, proceeding under convoy to Ostend with band playing "God Save the King." Amelia and Jos proceeded to Ramsgate for passage to Ostend. Timeline note: opening summer of 1815; Napoleon preparing behind frontier-fortresses while English army presents orderly, prosperous appearance.
- **Primary Locations**: London (Russell Square, Thames Street counting-house, Slaughters' hotel, Gray's Inn Square, Cavendish Square fine hotel, Hulker and Bullock bankers on Lombard Street), Brighton (George-Amelia honeymoon, Rawdon-Rebecca residence, Ship Inn, bathing machines on beach), Mirecombe (Seena Orlwood—drowned in flood; Pebin Wexwood, Maric Lindson, Rozek Hollwood, Halan Hollwood, Isbin Hollwood, Orvie, Nynelle Stenworth, Seena Hollett, Brenelle and Orvie Hollett, Thidrek Corrett, Feten Lindner, children of Quenwick, Old Maric, Ilena Orlwood, Orrine, Staveton), Coldcombe hill farms, Dunholt village (Daric Brackwood, Thivie, Feena Stenworth, Cotho Brackwood, daughter Dalde Brackwood born), Chatham (embarkation point, inn with sitting-room prepared; 150th regiment mess; Mrs. O'Dowd's apartments where festive assembly held), Harwich (shipping departure point), Fulham (Mrs. Sedley's house, Mr. and Mrs. Clapp, Irish servant Miss Flannigan, Mr. Clapp gardening), Ramsgate (departure point for Ostend packets), Ostend (destination), Brussels (military balls planned), Belgium (destination; flat, flourishing, easy country with green fields, quiet cities, wide chaussees, canal-boats, rich pastures, pleasant villages, old chateaux), Bryngate market town (Colan Lindson, Tassa Brackwood—newly wed, living there; baker's boy; forge; well; turnip cart; stall with ribbons), Salford (Thiena Hollwood and Ridan Corrett residence; son Ortho Corrett born; family living there).

## Main Characters

**Captain William Dobbin** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Brighton and London Actions - COMPLETED**: Arrived via Slaughters' hotel; witnessed Ensign Stubble's tears; dined with officers at theatre box. At Ship Inn: assumed "jovial and rattling manner" hiding feelings upon seeing Amelia; made clumsy compliments. In George's room: delivered lawyer's letter of disinheritance; George erupted blaming Dobbin; Dobbin offered personal financial support, promised not to forget godson in will; George forgave him. Evening dinner: assumed character of "rattle"; described Belgium fetes and fashion; when Rebecca announced intention to go to Belgium on staff, Dobbin flushed red, objected about danger, became "very confused and silent."
- **Cavendish Square Hotel - COMPLETED**: Attempted to remonstrate after dinner against extravagance of turtle and champagne for archbishop; George dismissed concerns. Dobbin walked home to Slaughters' musing about being in hackney-coach with Mrs. Osborne.
- **Chatham Arrival - COMPLETED**: At Chatham inn, wearing shells on frockcoat, crimson sash and sabre; paced street for an hour past in expectation of friends' arrival; presented military appearance that made Jos proud to claim his acquaintance. Recognized friendly countenance by Amelia upon her arrival.
- **Mrs. O'Dowd's Party - COMPLETED**: Never spoke to Amelia during whole evening. Took Jos home from party (Jos in maudlin state); Jos told tiger-hunt story with great effect to Mrs. O'Dowd and at mess-table. Handed Amelia into carriage as she departed; she rebuked him smilingly for not taking notice of her all night. Loitered smoking cigar before inn door long after, watched lights vanish from George's sitting-room windows and shine out in bedroom; did not return to quarters until almost morning. Could hear cheering from ships in river where transports were taking in cargoes preparatory to dropping down Thames.
- **Embarkation - COMPLETED**: Departed with regiment on transports proceeding under convoy to Ostend.
- **Internal Conflict**: Deeply troubled by guilt over hastening marriage; feels his own unendurable suspense drove him to crush uncertainty; considers himself traitor to both father and son. Secret adoration of Amelia is now his "greatest privilege and hope of life"; privately resolved he would not have let her go to Belgium if married to her; will not remonstrate with George as master. Knows Amelia considers him plain, awkward, ungainly; acquiesces humbly; acknowledges "a time came when she knew him better" but that was distant.
- **Reputation**: "Greatly respected in the regiment, as the best officer and the cleverest man in it"
- **Piano Purchase**: Bought piano for Amelia's father's house at Fulham

**George Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Status - MARRIED, DISINHERITED**: Married Amelia late April without father's consent; honeymoon at Brighton; disinherited by father's lawyer letter (determination "final and irrevocable"). Receives £2,000 in 4 percent annuities and £100/year widow's allowance for Amelia.
- **Financial Crisis - ACUTE**: Lost £140 to Rawdon Crawley at cards; gave substantial payment to Rawdon from bank-notes and bill on agents. Hotel bill and card losses "almost drained the young man's purse." Obtained £2,000 cheque from Hulker and Bullock bankers; gloated over sum. Fred Bullock (cadaverous suitor of George's sister Jane) turned deadly colour and slunk away upon seeing George at bankers.
- **Lawyer Visit - COMPLETED**: Upon arrival in London, wrote to father's solicitors requesting interview. Appeared before Mr. Higgs (attorney) expecting compromise message; met with "chilling coolness and indifference"; Higgs calculated £2,000 stock at rate of day; offered choice of cheque or purchased stock. George demanded cheque with "Damn the shillings and halfpence, sir," flattering himself he had put the old quiz to blush; stalked out with paper in pocket.
- **Banking - COMPLETED**: Proceeded to Hulker and Bullock bankers on Lombard Street; received his money; gloated over sum, never having had such amount before.
- **Chatham Status - COMPLETED**: Sent Amelia once more in carriage to her mother with strict orders and carte blanche to purchase everything requisite for lady of Mrs. George Osborne's fashion going on foreign tour. Paid Amelia's purchases with cheques on his agents "with the splendour of a lord." Highly pleased with his day's business. Received triangular billet on pink paper from Mrs. Major O'Dowd addressed to Mrs. Captain Osborne, sealed with dove and olive branch in light blue sealing wax, written in large undecided female hand. George recognized "Peggy O'Dowd's fist" by kisses on seal. Directed Amelia must attend small friendly party that very evening; said she must make acquaintance with regiment there. Noted O'Dowd goes in command of regiment, "and Peggy goes in command."
- **Mrs. O'Dowd's Party - COMPLETED**: Presented his lady to Mrs. Major O'Dowd. Laughed at her vivacity. Proud of Amelia's popularity at regiment party; pleased with manner in which she received gentlemen's attentions; glowed with pleasure at observing her affectionately watching him. Very carefully shawled his wife after party and brought her away from Mrs. O'Dowd's after general handshaking from young officers, who accompanied her to fly and cheered that vehicle as it drove off.
- **Embarkation - COMPLETED**: Departed with regiment on transports to Ostend.
- **Expectations and Character**: Believes father will relent before long. Determines that if personal merits fail, he will distinguish himself prodigiously in ensuing campaign so old gentleman must give in. Reflects "the world was before him" and luck might change at cards; calculates "a deal of spending in two thousand pounds." Said with respect to his brother-in-law Jos that his regiment marched with an elephant (amusing them by Jos's military airs).

**Amelia Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Emotional Crisis - RESOLVED**: Initially troubled by Rebecca's wit and accomplishments; misgives about Rebecca; observed George suffering ennui; tormented by guilt about forcing marriage and causing disinheritance. Face cleared reading disinheritance letter; idea of sharing poverty with beloved pleasant.
- **Resolution to Go to Belgium - EXECUTED**: Cried with "greatest spirit" determination to accompany George. Rose early morning; packed little trunks with "greatest alacrity" while George lay in bed.
- **Fulham Visit - COMPLETED**: Made "little disappointed curtsey" when George declined accompanying her. Went sadly down great staircase; Dobbin handed her into hackney-coach. Mother Mrs. Sedley clasped her to heart with "all maternal eagerness and affection," ran out of door weeping; old Mr. Clapp shrank back alarmed in shirt-sleeves; Irish servant-lass rushed up smiling "God bless you"; Amelia could hardly walk along flags.
- **Evening at Fulham - COMPLETED, MOOD TRANSFORMED**: Went upstairs to little room occupied before marriage; sank into chair; fell to thinking over past week; reflected on Rebecca's "twinkling green eyes and baleful smile"; indulged in usual mood of selfish brooding and listless melancholy; thought with terror of great funereal damask pavilion awaiting her at grand hotel; knelt by bedside seeking spiritual consolation. However, when tea was announced, came downstairs "a great deal more cheerful"; did not despond or deplore fate or think about George's coldness or Rebecca's eyes. Kissed father and mother; talked to old gentleman making him more merry than he had been for many a day. Sate down at piano (purchased by Dobbin) and sang all her father's favourite old songs. Pronounced tea excellent and praised exquisite taste in which marmalade was arranged in saucers. In determining to make everybody else happy, found herself so; was sound asleep in funereal pavilion; woke up with smile when George arrived from theatre.
- **Shopping Expedition - COMPLETED**: Sent by George once more in carriage to her mother with strict orders and carte blanche to purchase everything requisite for lady of Mrs. George Osborne's fashion going on foreign tour. Had but one day to complete outfit. Bustling about from milliner to linen-draper, escorted back to carriage by obsequious shopmen or polite owners. Mrs. Sedley was herself again almost, sincerely happy for first time since misfortunes. Amelia not at all above pleasure of shopping, bargaining, seeing and buying pretty things; gave herself little treat obedient to husband's orders; purchased quantity of lady's gear, showing great deal of taste and elegant discernment.
- **Mrs. O'Dowd's Party - COMPLETED**: Recognized lady as one of whom her husband had so often laughed. Grasped Amelia's hand very warmly. Presented to other female relations at tea-time; being quiet, good-natured, and not too handsome, made rather agreeable impression until arrival of gentlemen from mess, who all admired her so that sisters began to find fault with her. Had "little triumph, which flushed her spirits and made her eyes sparkle." Resolved in her heart: "I will make all his friends welcome. I will love all as I love him. I will always try and be gay and good-humoured and make his home happy." Adopted by regiment with acclamation. Captains approved, Lieutenants applauded, Ensigns admired. Old Cutler (Doctor) made professional jokes; Cackle (Assistant M.D. of Edinburgh) examined her upon literature, tried her with three best French quotations. Young Stubble went about whispering "Jove, isn't she a pretty gal?" and never took eyes off her except when negus came in. Gave Dobbin her little hand as she got out of carriage departing party, rebuked him smilingly for not having taken any notice of her all night.
- **Embarkation - IN PROGRESS**: Agreed to escort with Jos to Ramsgate where plenty of packets plying; had speedy passage to Ostend. Traveled unencumbered while regimental baggage (including Mrs. O'Dowd's bird of paradise and turban) went with bulk of goods.
- **Attitude to War**: Not much alarmed about ensuing war; Bonaparty to be crushed almost without struggle. Held him in utter contempt; took her opinions from those surrounding her, being too humble-minded to think for itself. Acquitted herself with considerable liveliness and credit on her first appearance in genteel world of London.

**Mrs. Major Peggy O'Dowd** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- One of five sisters and eleven children of noble house of Glenmalony
- Ordered her cousin Mick O'Dowd to marry her when she was about thirty-three years of age after trying nine seasons at Dublin and two at Bath and Cheltenham without finding partner for life
- Mick obeyed and carried her off to West Indies to preside over ladies of regiment into which he had just exchanged
- **Mrs. O'Dowd's Party - COMPLETED**: Sent Amelia triangular billet on pink paper sealed with dove and olive branch in light blue sealing wax, requesting her company that very evening to small friendly party. Received Amelia warmly; grasped her hand very warmly; greeted her with great vivacity. Told Amelia of her birth and pedigree; expressed intention that George should have been brother and sister Glorvina would have suited him; determined to take Amelia as sister instead and love her as one of family; assured her they would agree. Dispatched Ensign Simple to Colonel Tavish with message that Captain Osborne has brought his brother-in-law down and will bring him to 150th mess at five o'clock sharp. Remarked: "Hould your tongue, Mick, you booby. Them husbands are always in the way"; warned Mick (doctor) about propriety; intended to tell Amelia about regiment when alone. Introduced Jos to herself and Mick. Gossiped at tea-time about George's reformed rake status and Amelia's position as his wife. Inquired about Mrs. Kirk's evangelical questions to Amelia; presented penny books: "Howling Wilderness," "Washerwoman of Wandsworth Common," and "British Soldier's best Bayonet." Assisted Jos in learning military names and affairs. Jos received her assistance with great assiduity.
- **Embarkation - IN PROGRESS**: Bulk of her goods and chattels, including famous bird of paradise and turban, went with regimental baggage; proceeded with Jos and Amelia.
- Remarks suggest she goes in command of her husband despite his rank

**Major Mick O'Dowd** [MINOR CHARACTER]
- Served sovereign in every quarter of world; paid for every step in profession by acts of daring and gallantry
- Most modest, silent, sheep-faced and meek of little men; obedient to wife as if tay-boy
- At mess-table sits silently and drinks great deal; when full of liquor, reels silently home
- Speaks only to agree with everybody on every conceivable point; passes through life in perfect ease and good-humour
- Hottest suns of India never heated his temper; Walcheren ague never shook it
- Walked up to battery with same indifference as to dinner-table; dined on horse-flesh and turtle with equal relish
- Had old mother, Mrs. O'Dowd of O'Dowdstown; never disobeyed her except when ran away and enlisted and when persisted in marrying "that odious Peggy Malony"

**John Osborne (Old Mr. Osborne)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Wealthy merchant; George's father; savage, determined man
- **Disinheritance - EXECUTED AND COMMUNICATED**: Upon learning George married Amelia, erupted in fury. Retreated to study; locked door; retrieved mahogany escritoire containing all George's documents since childhood; examined papers with "curses quivering on livid lips" and "horrid hatred and disappointment"; marked, docketed, catalogued with dates. Commissioned lawyer to draft letter stating determination "final and irrevocable." George ceases to be member of family; Money expended upon George in minority exceeds entitlement (£2,000 in 4 percent annuities); Mr. Osborne waives all claim upon George's estate. Letter delivered via Mr. Chopper to Dobbin.
- **Frederick Bullock Information**: Fred Bullock dines every day in Russell Square now; told old Osborne of George's appearance at lawyers—came in "bold as brass" and "drawn out every shilling." Osborne swore with great oath that he little cared when or how soon George spent it.

**Jos Sedley** [MAJOR CHARACTER - EXPANDING ROLE]
- **Brighton Character**: Swaggering; described by Rebecca as better companion than sheriff's officers; potential source of funds.
- **Chatham Actions - COMPLETED**: Arrived in fine carriage at Chatham inn with Amelia. Recognized friendly countenance of Captain Dobbin. Jos attended Mrs. O'Dowd's party in maudlin state; told tiger-hunt story with great effect both at mess-table and soiree to Mrs. O'Dowd in her turban and bird of paradise. Dobbin and Captain Porter of 150th took him home to hotel.
- **Military Ambitions - DEVELOPING**: Agreed to escort sister Amelia and Mrs. Major O'Dowd abroad. Ceased shaving upper lip upon agreeing to escort. At Chatham followed parades and drills with great assiduity. Listened with utmost attention to conversation of his "brother officers" (as he called them in after days); learned many military names. Received excellent assistance from Mrs. O'Dowd in these studies. Made appearance in braided frock-coat and duck trousers, with foraging cap ornamented with smart gold band. Had carriage with him; informed everybody on board Lovely Rose confidentially that he was going to join Duke of Wellington's army. Folks mistook him for great personage, commissary-general, or government courier at very least. His courage prodigious; cried "Boney attack us!"; assured "poor Emmy" (Amelia) of no danger; explained allied military superiority with detailed knowledge of three hundred thousand Russians under Wittgenstein and Barclay de Tolly, five hundred thousand Austrians under Schwartzenberg and Prince Charles, Prussians under Prince Marshal. Treated young officers with sumptuosity; amusing them by military airs. Favoured with regiment.
- **Current Status - EMBARKED**: On Lovely Rose to Ostend with Amelia and Mrs. O'Dowd.

**Rebecca Sharp (Mrs. Rebecca Rawdon Crawley)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- **Miss Crawley Reconciliation - PERMANENTLY FAILED**: Successfully reconciled with Miss Briggs on beach. Initiated letter-writing campaign: Rawdon dictated (Rebecca composed) tender letter expressing humble acceptance of marriage, desire for reconciliation before departure. Miss Crawley recognized Rebecca's composition not Rawdon's; concluded "that little serpent of a governess who rules him"; believed all relatives want her dead for money. Despite Briggs' reports of letter touching her, Miss Crawley remained unmoved.
- **Meeting with Rawdon and Miss Crawley - EXECUTED, DISAPPOINTING OUTCOME**: Rawdon met Miss Crawley on Cliff when she took air in chair; she held out couple of fingers with "smiling and good-humoured air." Rawdon turned red as scarlet. Miss Crawley subsequently remarked to Briggs: "Rawdon is getting very fat and old...His nose has become red...His marriage to that woman has hopelessly vulgarised him...he smelt of gin abominably."
- **Miss Crawley's Final Refusal**: Declined to receive Rebecca; instructed Briggs to write letter stating her health too delicate for family discussions; thanked Rawdon for coming; instructed him to call upon her lawyer in Gray's Inn Square. Letter's reference to lawyer provided Rawdon some consolation after disappointment.
- **Monetary Scheme - EXECUTED**: Sent crumpled family-note to Rawdon requesting money from "Cupid" (George) before departure; Rawdon extracted considerable payment from George in bank-notes and bill on agents. Rebecca remarked to Rawdon: "A comfortable inn in Brighton is better than a spunging-house in Chancery Lane"; noted Mr. Jos and Captain Cupid are better companions than sheriff's officers.
- **Debtor Evasion - EXECUTED**: Packed all chief valuables and sent them off under care of George's servant on coach back to London.
- **Current Status**: In London with Rawdon. Status regarding General Tufto's staff or Belgium journey unclear; not mentioned among those embarking to Ostend.

**Rawdon Crawley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Secretly married to Rebecca; heavily indebted
- **Money Extraction - EXECUTED**: Sent crumpled family-note requesting money from George; extracted considerable payment in bank-notes and bill on agents; lost £140 to George at cards
- **Miss Crawley Meeting - COMPLETED, EMOTIONALLY MOVED BUT REJECTED**: Met Miss Crawley when she took air in chair; she held out couple of fingers; Rawdon turned red as scarlet with rapture and confusion. Miss Crawley subsequently disparaged his appearance, character, and drinking. Went to Gray's Inn Square to visit Miss Crawley's lawyer; "came back furious" to Rebecca in London
- **Current Status**: In London, furious after lawyer visit. Not mentioned among those embarking to Ostend.

## Critical Facts and Status

- **MILITARY CAMPAIGN - ACTIVATED AND UNDERWAY**: Regiment ordered to Belgium; embarkation completed. Two days after Mrs. O'Dowd's festive assembly at her apartments, amid cheering from all East India ships in river and military on shore, band playing "God Save the King," officers waving hats, crews hurrahing gallantly, transports went down river and proceeded under convoy to Ostend. Amelia, Jos, and Mrs. O'Dowd drove to Ramsgate unencumbered and had speedy passage to Ostend on packets. Belgium described as flat, flourishing, easy country with green fields, quiet cities, wide chaussees, canal-boats gliding by rich pastures and pleasant villages, old chateaux lying amongst old trees, crowded with well-to-do English travellers. Soldiers paid their scores at village inns; Highlanders billeted in Flemish farm-houses. Appeared brilliant and harmless as Hyde Park review. Timeline: opening summer of 1815; Napoleon screened behind frontier-fortresses, preparing outbreak to drive all orderly people into fury and blood.
- **GEORGE-AMELIA MARRIAGE - ESTABLISHED IN BELGIUM**: Married late April; disinheritance "final and irrevocable"; both determined to go to Belgium together. George obtained £2,000 cheque from solicitors; gloated over money. Amelia emotionally stabilized; completed shopping for foreign tour with great taste and discernment. Both attended and succeeded at Mrs. Major O'Dowd's party; Amelia enjoyed triumph as regiment unanimously admired her; resolved to make George's home happy and welcome all his friends. Now both in Belgium.
- **REBECCA-MISS CRAWLEY RECONCILIATION - PERMANENTLY FAILED**: All reconciliation attempts rebuffed; Miss Crawley refused Rebecca and Rawdon; sent Rawdon to lawyer with negative outcome; disparaged Rawdon's appearance and habits. Rebecca and Rawdon in London, not proceeding to Belgium.
- **FINANCIAL CRISIS - ACUTE ONGOING**: George disinherited; must live on captain's pay and £100/year widow's allowance; obtained £2,000 cheque but had already spent substantially on hotel bills and card losses; paid Amelia's shopping with cheques on agents. Rawdon and Rebecca evaded creditors in Brighton; sent valuables to London; status of their debts ongoing.
